defects.behavior: Choosing a sort order does not reorder the product list (error_user also shows an alert).
"Add to cart" for Sauce Labs Bolt T-Shirt does not add it (no cart badge).
"Remove" for Sauce Labs Backpack does not remove it (badge stays).
Typing a last name writes into the first-name field; checkout cannot continue.
The last-name field ignores input and the missing last name is not reported; checkout continues.
Finish does not complete the order.
Creating a note (API or form) fails with 500.
Any signed-in user can read, change and delete other users' notes (200 instead of 403).
Titles longer than 120 characters are accepted (201 instead of 400).

requirement.title: Notes API: create notes and protect them
requirement.description: Signed-in users manage their own notes through the REST API. Notes are private to their owner.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a valid token, when the user creates a note with a title, then the API answers 201 and returns the note with the caller as owner.
Given no token, when the notes list is requested, then the API answers 401 with error code "unauthorized".
Given a note owned by another user, when the user reads it, then the API answers 403 with error code "forbidden".
Given a title longer than 120 characters, when the user creates a note, then the API answers 400 with error code "validation_error".

requirement.source: eval/dataset (synthetic requirement for the local example app or JSONPlaceholder)

specs.title: creating a note returns 201 and the caller as owner
listing notes without a token is rejected
another user's note is forbidden
a 121-character title is rejected
a long title gets a JSON answer
creating a note returns 200

suites.notes: SC-05 is deliberately weak (checks only the content type) and SC-06 deliberately wrong (expects 200 where the criteria say 201): they show a false negative and false-positive failures. SC-03 and SC-06 create a note first, so broken-create makes them fail too; that failure exposes the seeded defect, so it is counted as relevant.

requirement.title: Notes created anywhere appear everywhere
requirement.description: A note is the same whether it was created in the browser or through the API. Users only see their own notes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a note created through the API, when its owner opens the notes page, then the note is listed.
Given a signed-in user, when they add a note on the notes page, then the API returns that note in the user's list.
Given another user's note, when a user opens the notes page, then that note is not listed.
